newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta strengthens vs mark, struggles at 83.40.
newsitem.headline: Peseta strengthens vs mark, struggles at 83.40.

text.p: The peseta strengthened against the mark in late trade on Thursday, boosted by dollar gains, ignoring the Bank of Spain's decision to reduce rates.
By 1700 GMT, the peseta was still strong, but had given up its attempt to break through resistance at 83.40 per mark to trade at 83.48/49 from 83.65/68 late on Wednesday.
"There has been a little bit of everything. The peseta managed to break 83.52 and touched a maximum of 83.42 per mark before ceding slightly on light profit-taking," a dealer said.
The Bank of Spain cut it's key money market rate 25 basis points to 6.00 percent, but this had little effect on the Spanish currency.
Traders said they had not seen the central bank intervening in the market since Friday when the peseta broke through the key 84.00 per mark barrier.
